chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Thumāmah, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī, peace be upon him: “I wish to remain in Makkah and al-Madīnah, but I have a debt upon me, so what do you say?”
He said: “Return to the place of paying your debt, and see to it that you meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while no debt remains upon you, for the believer does not betray.”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: The believer, characterized here by faithfulness to obligations.
key_terms.اِرْجِعْ: Return; here, a command to go back in order to fulfill one’s obligation.
key_terms.تَلْقَى اللَّهَ: To meet Allah; a reference to one’s final standing before Him.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A financial debt or obligation owed by a person.
key_terms.لَا يَخُونُ: Does not betray; does not violate trust or fail in owed responsibilities.
key_terms.مُؤَدَّى: The place or act of rendering and paying what is due.

ai.seo_question: Should a person delay paying debt in order to stay in Makkah or Madinah?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs a believer to prioritize settling debts before choosing to remain in honored places such as Makkah and Madinah. It emphasizes that meeting Allah without the liability of unpaid debt is part of the believer’s integrity, because a true believer does not betray trusts and obligations.
